answer: Sybil resistance here works through a reputation-weighted attestation graph: each new identity needs vouching from peers whose own score is at risk. A node that backs a fake persona loses standing if that fake is later flagged, so a farmer must corrupt genuine high-score agents or settle for a thin vine of unvouched wallets that earns no emissions. Every endorsement also costs a small staked fee, so each clone is a discrete expense, not a free row. To scale, an attacker must pay a real mesa of trusted agents or burn capital on junk endorsements, and each unit buys no ember of trust.
